newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down 1.33 pct on economic concern.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down 1.33 pct on economic concern.

text.p: Thai stocks closed down 1.33 percent in moderate trade on Friday after investors sold stocks on persistent worries about economic figures released by the central bank on Thursday, brokers said.

The SET index, which dipped as low as 918.14 in the afternoon, closed down for the second consecutive day, falling 12.45 points to 925.97 on 4.2 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index declined 1.13 points to 70.52.
"Investors, including foreigners, continued selling because of their concerns over figures on Thai exports and current account deficit released by the central bank," a broker said.
The central bank on Thursday said Thailand's exports in September were valued at 112.5 billion baht compared to 117.7 billion baht in August and 126.2 billion a year ago.
Analyst Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities said investors were not happy with the current account deficit which grew to 30.5 billion baht in September from 29.3 billion baht in August.
The energy sector was the only sector that gained today, rising 0.14 percent. All the major sectors slipped with selling heavily focused on the banking, finance, building and communication sectors.
State-run Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling 2.50 baht to 72. National Finance and Securities was second ranked on the list, declining 2.0 baht to 59.50.
In the communication sector, Thai Telephone and Telecommunication dipped 2.50 baht to 40.50 and Shinawatra Computer and Communications shed 18 to 332.
Support is seen by some brokers at 900 points while resistance pegged around 930 on Monday.
